reading.body:
H.R. 9442 is a one-party bill: its sponsor and all twenty cosponsors are Democrats, and no recorded vote is listed.

The support is entirely from one caucus, which tells you the bill is a statement of position rather than a measure with a path to passage. The cosponsor list is long enough to show the moratorium idea has a real bloc behind it, and short enough to show that bloc is confined to a single party.

The bill's own text tags energy and data centers and uses preemption language about state law. That is the mechanism that matters for AI: a moratorium on data centers is a constraint on where compute can be built, and preemption language is a fight over whether states or Congress set that constraint. The three lobbying filings naming the bill, from Network and the Business Software Alliance, show the software industry is already tracking it. A filing that names a bill shows the bill was an issue in the lobbying, not the position taken on it.

The data does not say what the bill would do in operative detail, whether it has moved beyond introduction, or how the two lobbying firms stand on it. It also does not cover state-level moratoriums, which the linked siting and power law section addresses separately.

summary: H.R. 9442, Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act. Latest status date 2026-06-24. Issues tagged from the bill's own text: energy and data centers. Its text uses preemption language about state law. 3 lobbying filing(s) for 2025 or later name it.
